problem_sentence: When a hint-conditioned teacher model guides the student, the teacher can learn to lean on the hint so heavily that its reasoning is impossible for the student to imitate.
quote: If the teacher relies too strongly on privileged context, it may assign high probability mass to reasoning that the student cannot reproduce from its own observations. The teacher distribution can also become overly concentrated or simply drift too far from the student, making optimization unstable.

problem_sentence: It is unknown whether a model's hidden states can predict its score when the grader is a rubric or another model rather than a clean right/wrong check.
quote: Third, we trained our estimator on verifiable rewards, but many non-verifiable tasks are instead scored by rubrics or generative judges [Gunjal et al., 2025, Su et al., 2026]. Whether a baseline for such graded and noisier rewards can likewise be predicted from internal states remains open.

problem_sentence: It is untested whether a probe on hidden states keeps tracking the policy's value over very long training runs as the policy drifts.
quote: Our experiments are conducted under a fixed compute budget, and while the trends we report are consistent across backbones and benchmarks, characterizing the behavior of internal state value estimation under substantially longer training horizons remains an interesting direction that we leave to future work with greater compute resources.

problem_sentence: The step-level credit depends on an external text-embedding model, so the method inherits whatever that embedding model gets wrong about which actions are similar.
quote: HPO constructs intent distributions in a semantic embedding space, so a natural question is whether its step-level advantage estimates are sensitive to the particular embedding model used to represent state–action pairs.

problem_sentence: The hierarchical multi-turn RL method was mostly tested on a tiny GPT-2 model, so whether its gains hold on modern LLMs is unverified.
quote: Due to the computational constraints associated with running many trials of multiple RL algorithms and ArCHer instantiations, we had to conduct most of our experiments with a relatively small GPT-2 architecture.

problem_sentence: Turn-level PPO was shown to work on only two text-simulated benchmarks, not on real web agents with rich tools or physical environments.
quote: we only evaluate our methods on two representative datasets, one for web-based agents and one for embodied agents. In the embodied setting, we primarily consider text-simulated environments.

problem_sentence: The approach was validated only on ALFWorld and WebShop with small models and sparse end rewards, so its value on bigger, richer, or asynchronous agent tasks is unknown.
quote: We do not study settings with dense process rewards, mixed reward sources, continuous, asynchronous interaction, or substantially larger and more diverse agent domains. Further validation is needed to determine whether the same temporal estimator remains beneficial in richer long-horizon environments.

problem_sentence: The delayed-credit signal is only computed for a narrow class of turns (non-improving turns before the first success), so other turns get no benefit from hindsight.
quote: Since both hindsight estimation and counterfactual selection are restricted to bi,k = 1, delayed credit is zero for turns with immediate improvement and for post-success keep or regression turns.

problem_sentence: Academic groups cannot afford RL experiments above 7B parameters, so whether turn-level rewards still help at production scale is untested.
quote: our experiments are restricted to models no larger than 7B parameters due to the computation budget. It is prohibitively expensive to perform large-scale RL experiments for LLMs, and unfortunately, we do not have enough resources to demonstrate the impact of GTPO on larger models.

problem_sentence: The turn-level reward scheme has only been shown on math with code execution, not on real software engineering agents.
quote: this work has mainly focused on Tool-Integrated Reasoning tasks, but the idea of GTPO can be broadly applicable for improving models’ reasoning capability in general multi-turn scenarios such as real-world software engineering tasks, which we leave to future work.

problem_sentence: It is unknown how finely a response should be chopped into segments for the critic to score, and the method is untested outside math.
quote: Future directions include extension beyond mathematical reasoning, decomposing and designing better In-Context Conditioning prompt, and deciding optimal segmentation granularity.

problem_sentence: Pretrained vision-language models misperceive basic game elements, so RL alone cannot start and a hand-curated supervised dataset has to be built first for each new environment.
quote: they may struggle to distinguish Mario from enemies or to accurately identify their spatial positions. We therefore begin with a light supervised fine-tuning (SFT) stage to inject domain-specific knowledge and improve environment-specific perception.

problem_sentence: When training on several tasks at once, easier tasks produce longer episodes and therefore more training tokens, so they silently dominate the update unless sampling is rebalanced.
quote: because different levels can vary substantially in difficulty, uniform level sampling can lead to an undesirable imbalance in the optimization objective. In particular, trajectories from easier levels tend to be longer, since the agent can naturally survive and progress further.

problem_sentence: The theory behind the critic mini-batch size recommendation assumes rollouts are independent, which is false when they share a prompt or when weights come from the same group.
quote: The variance identity assumes independent rollout contributions; correlated rollouts or weights estimated jointly from a group may change this scaling.

problem_sentence: The negative verdict on step-level credit comes from one text environment, one model family, and offline LoRA training, so it is unknown whether it holds in richer settings.
quote: the audit runs in a single environment with a binary outcome, and every claim is scoped accordingly. The training-loop experiments are single-family and single-scale (Qwen2.5-7B, LoRA (low-rank adaptation), offline)

problem_sentence: The 50% pass-rate target is derived only for pass/fail rewards with eight rollouts per task, so it is unknown what the right operating point is for graded rewards or other group sizes.
quote: Our claims are scoped to binary-reward RLVR with grouped rollouts, and all main experiments use N = 8 rollouts per task.

problem_sentence: Training data that shows the reasoning behind a software fix, not just the fix, is expensive to collect, while bare question-answer pairs are plentiful.
quote: While datasets with explicit Chain of Thoughts (CoT) would significantly benefit learning, they are costly to obtain.

problem_sentence: The hints that drive the whole method come from a separate frontier model reading the gold patch, so the approach depends on having both a stronger external model and a reference solution.
quote: The compressed trajectory, together with the corresponding ground-truth patch, is then provided as input to an expert model (DeepSeek v3), which produces textual hints identifying the causes of failure.

problem_sentence: Adding failed trajectories to the progress estimator's memory helps on one benchmark and hurts on another, and there is no rule for when to include them.
quote: On WebShop, mean success is lower at both model sizes; task score decreases at 1.5B but increases slightly at 7B. The effect of failure examples therefore varies across benchmarks and model sizes.

problem_sentence: The widely used multi-turn GRPO implementation weights long trajectories more heavily in the group baseline than the textbook formula does, a silent bias that methods built on it inherit.
quote: The base multi-turn implementation computes within-task outcome statistics over expanded turn rows. Consequently, a trajectory with more turns contributes more entries to the group mean and standard deviation. This convention differs from the standard estimator in Equation 1

problem_sentence: The variance-of-reward curriculum has only been tested with pass/fail grading; whether it works with graded or model-judged rewards is unverified.
quote: Learnability in prior work was only considered for binary rewards. Our Theorem 3.1 suggests that more generally, including for non-binary rewards, that maximising learnability, defined as the variance of the final reward, maximises expected model improvement. However, more experiments are needed to empirically verify this.

problem_sentence: The self-play agent could not write realistic natural-language bug reports; its generated issues collapsed to repetitive copies, so training is limited to formal test specifications unlike real user issues.
quote: our initial attempts failed to reliably generate high-quality and unambiguous issue descriptions. The generated issues tend to copy test patches, are logically incoherent, and collapse to identical patterns. We attribute this to limited natural language capabilities of our 32B base model (CWM) and the opaque reward signals that fail to promote quality or diversity.

problem_sentence: The self-generated task stream has no control over where bugs are placed, so it produces duplicates and skews toward certain parts of a codebase.
quote: Distribution control with seeding: The current approach lacks explicit control over bug injection locations, which can lead to duplicate bugs or distribution bias when sampling multiple times from the same repository.

problem_sentence: The method was only tested up to 7B and uses a fixed mix of replayed versus fresh data, with no rule for how that mix should change over training.
quote: Due to computational resource constraints, we did not conduct experiments on models exceeding 7B parameters; consequently, the performance gains of RSPO on larger-scale models remain to be fully validated. Additionally, the off-policy data ratio is kept constant throughout our experiments. Employing an adaptive ratio (e.g., a decaying schedule) could potentially enhance the final results.

problem_sentence: Replaying an agent's own past trajectories saves rollouts but does not raise the final score; the gain only appears when the replayed data comes from a differently-rewarded policy.
quote: we observed that when the amount of training data is held constant, using the model’s own historical trajectories does not outperform the original baseline. Its primary advantage lies in improving data usage efficiency rather than final performance.

problem_sentence: The benchmark stops the moment the agent is delivered, so it says nothing about maintaining it, handling changed requirements, or improving it from real traffic.
quote: Evaluation ends at submission: maintaining the agent after deployment, absorbing requirement changes, and learning from live traffic are natural extensions of the task we model, and we leave them to future work.

problem_sentence: Because the underlying domains are public, a model may already have memorized the answers from its training data instead of finding them in the provided documents, which inflates scores.
quote: The τ -bench domains we build on are public, so a developer could score well by recalling policy values from training data rather than recovering them from evidence.

problem_sentence: Training an agent to maximize task success against a simulated user may teach it to manipulate people, and the metrics used would not notice.
quote: Optimizing task rewards can favor manipulative or deceptive strategies (Williams et al., 2025). Our task-performance and simulator-fidelity metrics do not assess effects on user autonomy, trust, or long-term welfare.

problem_sentence: Fine-tuning the simulator on plain human chat logs makes it stop thinking out loud, and the fix of re-teaching reasoning from a small dataset may throw away abilities the base model already had.
quote: We find that this response-only supervision suppresses the model’s explicit reasoning behavior, which we subsequently restore through ThoughtTrace supervision followed by reinforcement learning. Although this staged procedure is effective, it may discard useful reasoning capabilities already present in the pretrained model before relearning them from a much smaller annotated dataset.

problem_sentence: The method needs a stock of past completed runs with known outcomes, so it cannot help on a brand-new benchmark that nobody has run yet.
quote: The framework therefore targets the common case of repeatedly evaluating evolving agents against a stable benchmark, where per-pass cost compounds across iterations, rather than the first-ever evaluation of a brand-new benchmark with no prior runs, for which no early-prediction signal yet exists.

problem_sentence: The collapse phenomenon has only been shown for two-party English text conversations, so it is unknown whether it also happens with groups, images, or other languages.
quote: All three settings are text-only, two-agent, English, and LLM-panel evaluated; whether the mechanism extends to N-agent populations, multimodal environments, or non-English settings remains open.

problem_sentence: Humans wrote the skills by hand, so the agent is only helped in situations the authors anticipated.
quote: The skill library is hand-designed and necessarily incomplete, so its benefits depend on whether the provided abstractions match the situations encountered by the agent.

problem_sentence: Even with skills the agents are nowhere near finishing the game, failing at precise moment-to-moment control, rare knowledge, long-term resource management, and strategy.
quote: Some failure modes include situations requiring fine-grained tactical control, rare game knowledge, long-term resource management, or strategic planning beyond what the current skills encode.

problem_sentence: Agents do not yet know when to rely on a big pre-built skill and when to drop down to fine-grained individual actions.
quote: To deal with these failures, future language agents will need to be able to proficiently move up and down the abstraction ladder by knowing when to use higher-level skills vs. when it’s more appropriate to use the low-level primitives (see Appendix C.2 for examples).

problem_sentence: Agents cannot yet write their own missing skills from repeated failures or build their own memory tools, so they keep re-reading an ever-growing history instead.
quote: Agents could identify repeated failures, implement missing action skills, and test and refine them through interaction [Liang et al., 2023, Wang et al., 2024]. Alongside these skills, they could construct tools that track previously observed entities and retrieve relevant information on demand, reducing the need to repeatedly process a growing observation history.

problem_sentence: Letting the agent use both skills and raw actions keeps most of the benefit but more than doubles the inference bill compared with skills alone.
quote: It occasionally exceeds skill-only performance, but raises average inference cost to 2.3x and token usage to 2x that of skills.

problem_sentence: The theory only proves the method beats the best fixed setting of the older approach, not a version of it that is re-tuned at every step.
quote: a comparison against the per-round retuned PP-SSL oracle P 1 t E[inf b Vt (1, b)] would require a dynamic-regret analysis, which we do not pursue.

problem_sentence: Training a model with verifiable-reward RL makes its single answers better but its many sampled answers more alike, so majority voting over them can get worse than before training.
quote: Training raises pass@1, but it spends the diversity the vote needs, and at a fixed inference budget the vote can end below where it started. The more votes a user draws, the larger the loss.

problem_sentence: The finding has only been checked with one RL algorithm, small models, and small voter counts, and the method only avoids damage rather than guaranteeing improvement.
quote: Our study covers one RL algorithm (GRPO), voter counts K ≤ 16, models up to 8B, and budgets of 16 to 160 votes. Thickets protect the vote rather than guarantee a gain over the base.

problem_sentence: As more and more answers are sampled, the untrained model keeps catching up, so the advantage of any RL-trained pool may vanish at large sampling budgets.
quote: Their lead over the base and over GRPO-single (matched) shrinks as the budget grows, and at 160 votes they beat the base in 9 of 16 settings. On Llama the base’s vote is still rising at 160 votes, so the lead may shrink further at larger budgets.

problem_sentence: Majority voting only works when answers can be compared exactly, so the method has only been shown on math and not on code or open-ended tasks.
quote: Majority voting needs comparable answers, so our voting results are math-only, and code enters only through coverage, pass@1, and correlation.

problem_sentence: Nobody checked whether the standard regularizer that keeps a trained model close to its starting point would have prevented the diversity loss.
quote: All arms train without a KL penalty (Table 4), and we do not test whether KL regularization changes the single adapter’s vote.

problem_sentence: Splitting the budget into only two pools gives unstable results that vary a lot from run to run.
quote: The two-member thicket is the least reliable configuration: it is the weakest thicket on three of four models and has the largest seed spread of any thicket entry in Table 1.

problem_sentence: The method was only tested on an 8-billion-parameter student, so nobody knows whether it still helps for much larger models.
quote: How LeAct interacts with frontier-scale students, beyond the 8B fixed here, is another direct extension.

problem_sentence: The method is only a supervised-learning recipe and has not been combined with online reinforcement learning, where the expert's actions could give step-by-step credit.
quote: the most direct algorithmic extension is merging LeAct with online RL, where the oracle’s action distribution can serve as a process-level baseline for credit assignment.

problem_sentence: The paper never compares against standard RL training, so it is unknown whether recovering expert reasoning beats simply doing RL.
quote: Two reasons we do not implement RL/policy-gradient baselines (e.g., GRPO [11]): this work targets SFT / mid-training, and C OT E X I T already approximates a coarse-grained REINFORCE through its rollout-and-bootstrap loop.

problem_sentence: The method reads the student's action probabilities from text it writes out rather than from its actual token probabilities, and the exact version has not been tested.
quote: Replacing the textual proxy with token-level log pθ (y | x, z) scoring is a straightforward substitution that we leave to future work; we do not expect the qualitative findings of §5 to change, since both estimators agree in expectation under a faithfully-trained policy line.

problem_sentence: Results are reported at whichever of three training rounds scored best, and the paper does not say how to decide when to stop in practice.
quote: Each round retains K=2 CoTs per state. C OT E X I T trains on the forward direction only (K|X | examples per round), while LeAct’s M-step jointly trains forward and backward directions (2K|X | per round). For each (method, setting) we report at the round (out of 3) with the best evaluation metric.

problem_sentence: The system only shows that long agent conversations fit in memory; it has not shown that training is faster, that the policy is better, or that the kernel computes exactly the same thing.
quote: These results support the narrower claim that environment, RL-dataflow, and attention-kernel integration can improve the memory feasibility of long-horizon agent training. They do not yet establish algorithmic superiority, broad generalization, exact implementation equivalence, or end-toend computational speedup.

problem_sentence: Only peak GPU memory was measured, so nobody knows whether the approach actually speeds up training.
quote: Because the experiment measures only peak VRAM, it does not establish improvements in throughput, latency, total training time, or accelerator utilization.

problem_sentence: The training result is a single run in one domain with no repeated seeds, so it is not known whether the improvement is real or luck.
quote: They also motivate broader evaluations across domains, random seeds, model scales, and training horizons to further characterize the robustness and generality of the observed improvements.

problem_sentence: The approach depends on tasks whose success can be checked by a program, so it does not directly apply to open-ended tasks without a built-in checker.
quote: First, our system is particularly well suited to agentic tasks that operate in controlled environments with programmatically verifiable outcomes. This setting is naturally instantiated by τ 2 -Bench, where the policy interacts with a user simulator, invokes domain tools, and receives feedback based on the resulting environment state.

problem_sentence: The benchmark uses only 153 items, so it cannot show the kinds of mistakes agents make with a realistically large catalog, and growing it while keeping items unseen by the model is unsolved.
quote: The catalog is intentionally small (153 titles) to isolate reasoning ability from retrieval scale — agents access it via API tools, so size is opaque to the model — but limits failure-mode diversity; scaling while preserving post-cutoff freshness is future work.

problem_sentence: The released benchmark only covers movie recommendation, so its conclusions may not hold for other recommendation domains.
quote: While the framework is domain-agnostic, our released benchmark covers movies only. Extending to other domains is straightforward given the typed-predicate scoring; cross-domain task suites and larger-𝑘 runs are natural next steps.

problem_sentence: Recommendation benchmarks have no way to guarantee the model has not already seen the items during training, unlike coding benchmarks that use only new problems.
quote: LiveCodeBench [10] and SciNUP [1] establish post-cutoff content as a contamination defense in code and scholarly domains but no recommendation analog exists.

problem_sentence: Letting the model think longer barely helps on this benchmark, so the bottleneck is something other than reasoning effort.
quote: DS V4 Flash gains only +0.025 pass^1 from non-thinking to max-effort thinking, suggesting current models are capability constrained for this benchmark.

problem_sentence: The agent asks all its questions in one shot, so the work says nothing about back-and-forth conversations, and the scores come from a model judge that may disagree with real people.
quote: Our single-turn design isolates clarification quality but does not capture multi-turn dynamics. The software engineering focus for empirical grounding provides domain-specific findings, although our methodology generalizes. Finally, the LLM judge enables scalable evaluation, but may diverge from human judgment.

problem_sentence: The small trained model spots obvious missing details but cannot connect a bug report's symptoms to the deeper code knowledge needed to ask the right question.
quote: The model struggles when underspecification requires deep code comprehension to detect—it can identify surface-level gaps but cannot bridge from issue symptoms to underlying implementation concepts as reliably as GPT-5 which is superior in this aspect.

problem_sentence: Small research agents lose track of information once the conversation gets long, which caps their performance.
quote: This gap highlights long-context utilization as a key limitation of small-scale agents, and we report both configurations for transparency.

problem_sentence: The key knobs of the training method were tuned on a single domain, so they may not transfer.
quote: The user simulator (DeepSeek-V3 for training, GPT-4.1 for evaluation) introduces a distribution shift. Our GTPO hybrid hyperparameters (γ=0.9, λ=0.3) were tuned on one domain.

problem_sentence: The simulated users are synthetic English voices, so conclusions about accents and other languages are only suggestive.
quote: Language and Speech: We evaluate English only using TTS rather than recorded speech. Accent findings via TTS personas should be interpreted as indicative rather than definitive.

problem_sentence: Agents that solve 85% of tasks over text solve only about a third of the same tasks over voice, and even less with noise and accents.
quote: Our evaluation reveals a substantial voice-text gap: while GPT-5 (reasoning) achieves 85%, voice agents reach only 31–51% under clean conditions and 26–38% under realistic conditions—retaining only 30–45% of text capability.

problem_sentence: Agents in the benchmark may search as many times as they like, whereas real deployments often allow only one or two searches, so the results may not reflect production constraints.
quote: whereas many real-world systems operate under one- or few-shot search constraints; under such limits, we expect retrieval configuration to play a more decisive role in performance.

problem_sentence: Even when given a terminal where they could take notes, frontier agents did not use it to organize what they learned, and it is unknown how to get them to.
quote: Our terminal-use setting warrants deeper investigation, particularly the role of write tools, as more deliberate agent designs may better exploit note-taking, state tracking, and knowledge reorganization to improve long-horizon reasoning.

problem_sentence: Agents cover for poor search by searching many more times, which keeps the success rate up but makes conversations slow and costly for real users.
quote: These tradeoffs show that weaker or noisier retrieval is often compensated for by increased search and tool usage, preserving success rates at the cost of higher latency and lower interaction efficiency.

problem_sentence: Long conversations with many retrieved documents overflow the agent's memory and nobody has worked out how best to compress them.
quote: We leave exploration of more sophisticated context management strategies (e.g., selective summarization or retrieval-aware compression) to future work.

problem_sentence: Training only works well with very large batches of rollouts, which makes each update expensive.
quote: Larger batch sizes provide more stable advantage estimation in GRPO, leading to better learning signals and improved performance across all metrics.

problem_sentence: The paper has no limitations section; the only self-critical statement is a generic impact note.
quote: We do not anticipate immediate negative societal impacts beyond those generally associated with more capable language agents, but careful monitoring and responsible release practices remain important as tool-using systems improve.

problem_sentence: Even a 128,000-token memory fills up on the hardest research tasks, so the agent needs a better way to manage what it remembers.
quote: First, the current 128K context length remains insufficient for handling the most complex long-horizon tasks, motivating further exploration of extended context windows or more advanced context management mechanisms (Qiao et al., 2025; Wu et al., 2025c).

problem_sentence: The agent was trained for one fixed prompt style and one fixed set of tools, so it is unclear how well it handles new tools or instructions.
quote: Finally, our current Deep Research training focuses on specific prompt instructions and predefined tool sets. We plan to enhance its robustness and extend the framework from Deep Research to broader agentic tool use scenarios.

problem_sentence: Combining several long research attempts into one bigger context to get a better answer is too expensive to compute.
quote: Given that DeepResearch involves multi-round tool calls and intensive reasoning, directly aggregating contexts from multiple trajectories is computationally prohibitive.

problem_sentence: The self-improving agent still does worse than the best hand-built commercial systems, and nobody knows whether running it longer would close the gap.
quote: However, it still falls short of closed-source SoTA SWE-bench solutions. An open question is whether running the DGM for longer would continue to yield performance gains and eventually surpass closed-source solutions.

problem_sentence: The system can only change its prompts and code around a frozen model, not the model's weights, so it is capped by what that model can already do.
quote: Since this version of the DGM is mainly powered by FMs, it is inherently limited by the capabilities of the underlying FM. Hence, an exciting future direction is to extend self-modification beyond just prompts or FM workflows, to include more computationally intensive methods, such as rewriting its own training script to update the FM itself.

problem_sentence: The whole approach assumes that scoring well on coding benchmarks is the same as being good at improving oneself, which has not been verified.
quote: A key assumption in this work is that coding benchmarks are a good reflection of the agent’s ability to self-improve, since the self-modification task requires the agent to modify its own codebase.

problem_sentence: Optimizing for benchmark scores ignores other qualities people care about such as robustness and interpretability.
quote: Our empirical focus on benchmark optimization may not capture all desirable properties (robustness, interpretability, or broader

problem_sentence: The rules for which past agents to keep and which to build on are fixed by humans and the system cannot improve them.
quote: Currently, the open-ended exploration process (i.e., archive maintenance, parent selection) is fixed and not modifiable by the DGM, which we leave as an avenue for future work.

problem_sentence: The method only learns useful lessons from purposeful attempts at tasks; aimless exploration produces notes that do not help.
quote: First, table 1 shows that although CER performs even better in offline + online settings, it requires the trajectories to be goal-oriented to distill high-quality experiences. The performance is limited if trajectories from random explorations are provided.

problem_sentence: The agent has nothing to draw on for its very first tasks, and the offline version depends on humans having written example runs beforehand.
quote: Also, CER needs to learn trajectory data before starting the task. In online setting, the framework may not be able to use trajectory learning in the initial decision. In offline setting, the humanannotated trajectory will be used for CER learning, but the trajectory data prepared in advance depends on the annotation of the human annotator.

problem_sentence: Much of the benefit comes from a web-specific shortcut, remembering URLs to jump to, so it is unclear whether the idea transfers to environments without such shortcuts.
quote: Secondly, the environment dynamics help much in web environments, as shown in section 5.7, partially because the agent can directly navigate to a specific page with its URL. It would be interesting to investigate how we can utilize the environment dynamics in other agent tasks, such as real-world navigation (Shridhar et al., 2021) in future work.

problem_sentence: Agents forget everything between tasks and re-explore the same website from scratch each time, because training them for each environment is too expensive.
quote: While training in each specific environment is costly, current language agents seldom have an efficient way to continually learn about the environment, so they need to explore the environment from scratch for every single task (Koh et al., 2024b).

problem_sentence: Lessons distilled from failed attempts can mislead the agent, so failures are hard to learn from.
quote: The possible reason could be that the successful trajectories have higher quality and are more informative, while the failed trajectories provide some misleading action sequences that will negatively influence the agent’s decision-making.

problem_sentence: Whether the agent noticed missing information is only checked in the first three turns, and question quality is scored by a crude embedding distance.
quote: Underspecificity detection is measured only within the first three turns, as models rarely recover if they fail to engage early. Question quality is approximated via latent vector changes that weigh all information equally, though models may prioritize details differently.

problem_sentence: Generating and running tests to pick among candidate patches is so costly that the authors cut that step out of the agent entirely to make training affordable.
quote: We removed the patch selection step that require rather expensive test generation and execution, so our scaffold is significantly simpler, faster, and less compute intensive than Agentless.

problem_sentence: Tasks that need several networked services talking to each other, or careful control over network traffic, are hard to express in the lightweight sandbox.
quote: Third, network isolation is functional but less flexible than Docker's networking stack, which may limit support for tasks requiring complex multi-host topologies or fine-grained traffic control.

problem_sentence: Searching at each step multiplies the number of model calls per training rollout, so the method buys better policies with more rollout compute, and on some tasks total training cost goes up.
quote: TSR introduces additional compute during rollout generation, although this cost is incurred only at training time and is partially offset by requiring fewer optimization steps to convergence.

problem_sentence: Searching too hard produces trajectories the current model would almost never have generated itself, and standard clipped policy-gradient updates cannot learn from data that far from the model, so more search eventually hurts.
quote: For B >= 20, the KL divergence exceeds 0.30 and performance degrades. Since these settings use equal or greater rollout compute than moderate beam widths, the degradation cannot be attributed to insufficient compute. It instead suggests that the selected trajectories are too far from the proposing policy for clipped PPO/GRPO-style updates to extract useful gradients.

problem_sentence: The method was shown only on small Qwen models up to 7B and on toy or simulated environments, so it is unknown whether the gains hold for larger models or realistic agent tasks.
quote: our main evaluation spans two model scales and three complementary environments, with additional experiments extending the study to ALFWorld and AppWorld and to a 7B model. Evaluating further model families and interaction settings remains an important direction for assessing the broader applicability of TSR.

problem_sentence: The stabilizer was only tested on dense models in normal precision with short-to-medium tasks; mixture-of-experts models, low-precision inference, and long agent episodes with sparse rewards all make the training-inference gap bigger and are untested.
quote: We study dense Transformer policies under standard precision and a fixed set of asynchronous pipeline designs. Future work should evaluate VCPO on MoE models (where routing can amplify mismatch), under more aggressive quantization (e.g., FP8), and in substantially longer-horizon agentic settings

problem_sentence: The variance-reducing baseline needs the size of each trajectory's gradient, which normally means running the expensive backward pass twice; even the optimized version still adds about a fifth to step time.
quote: A naive gradient-aware baseline requires two backward passes: one to compute per-sample gradient norms and a second to apply the resulting baseline, roughly doubling backward compute time at scale.

problem_sentence: The recipe was only tested on models up to 7 billion parameters, and the paper's own finding that the best choices change with model size means it may not transfer to frontier-scale models.
quote: Unknown behavior of much larger LLMs: Due to computational constraints, our study focuses on models up to 7B parameters. How the scale-aware recipe translates to the behaviors of massive LLMs remains an open question.

problem_sentence: Systematic RL studies are only affordable on cheap local simulators, because GUI and coding environments are computationally heavy and live web tasks cost too much in API calls to run the many rollouts RL needs.
quote: the computational overhead of GUI and code agents, coupled with the prohibitive API costs of open-web tasks, creates severe bottlenecks for the extensive environmental exploration. Therefore, TravelPlanner emerges as an ideal, scalable environment for studying agentic RL.

problem_sentence: Exploration methods that decide where to branch a rollout need extra per-token computation inside generation, which slows each training step and, at 7B scale, buys no accuracy over plain GRPO.
quote: ARPO's adaptive rollout requires calculating the entropy difference at each generation step to determine whether to branch new trajectories. While intuitive, this mechanism increases the time cost per step.

problem_sentence: Trained agents fix small local mistakes but do not go back and change an early decision when a later tool result shows it was a dead end; they push on and violate the user's hard constraints instead.
quote: LLMs still struggle with long-horizon dependencies where upstream decisions must be revised based on downstream observations. Addressing this bottleneck remains a highly promising direction for future work in agentic planning and reasoning.

problem_sentence: When a training rollout and a user-facing model share a GPU, one long rollout prompt can make users wait, and the usual request scheduler has no way to cap that interference.
quote: Standard request scheduling cannot bound the compute interference: a single rollout prefill chunk can delay serving decodes, and sustained rollout batches can starve serving prefills (analyzed in §6.2).

problem_sentence: Sending fresh model weights from the training cluster to a serving cluster in another datacenter takes minutes per update and gets worse with bigger models, which limits how often rollout GPUs elsewhere can be refreshed.
quote: Even with InfiniBand (which is uncommon across datacenters), it can take up to 145 s and grow quickly with model size, becoming a bottleneck for frequent weight synchronization.

problem_sentence: The memory split between serving and rollout is only re-planned once per training step, so a sudden spike in user traffic has to be handled by abruptly killing rollout requests and throwing their partial work away.
quote: This iteration-level budget stabilizes rollout memory usage under typical serving load, but it cannot react to sudden serving bursts.

problem_sentence: The communication libraries used for distributed training assume a fixed set of machines with identical layouts, but a shared serving fleet changes membership and uses different model sharding, so those libraries cannot be reused for weight sync.
quote: Existing communication systems [10, 33, 49, 66] assume fixed process groups with uniform sharding. Cooperative elasticity breaks both assumptions: serving GPUs may join or leave across RL steps, while training and serving can adopt different parallelism strategies.

problem_sentence: Changing one line of the reward function means restarting the whole training job and reloading the model, so each small fix costs five to ten minutes and researchers iterate slowly.
quote: Editing agent code or reward functions forces a full restart of the training process, reloading the model, reinitializing the inference engine, and discarding any in-flight episodes, so that even a trivial change, such as a reward coefficient change, costs 5-10 minutes.

problem_sentence: Each turn of a multi-turn agent repeats the entire earlier conversation, so if every model call is treated as its own training sample the trainer recomputes the same long prefix over and over.
quote: As an agent interacts with its environment over many turns, its conversation accumulates substantial redundancy (repeated system prompts, tool definitions, and observation histories), which the optimizer reprocesses on every policy-gradient update.

problem_sentence: Training frameworks assume one model is being trained, but real agent systems use several models of different sizes for different roles, and no standard trainer can update them together.
quote: Most current systems optimize a single policy at a time, whereas real-world agentic applications increasingly field heterogeneous teams in which different roles are backed by models of different sizes (e.g., a 7B executor alongside a 32B planner), each requiring its own trainable policy.

problem_sentence: Merging repeated conversation prefixes saves compute, but chat templates re-tokenize earlier turns differently (for example stripping thinking blocks), so merging by text can train on token sequences the model never actually produced.
quote: For the majority of timeline pairs, the two strategies produce identical results, but they diverge precisely at the boundary where researchers must trade training efficiency against train-inference (TI) consistency.

problem_sentence: The two common ways to spend extra inference compute both waste it: running many independent samples fills GPU memory and queues requests, while killing bad samples early leaves the GPU idle and does not make correct answers more likely.
quote: traditional parallel sampling treats traces independently and induces severe memory bottlenecks, while subtractive pruning starves hardware and fails to actively and sufficiently shift the output distribution.

problem_sentence: Generating hundreds of long reasoning attempts for one hard problem takes hours on a top GPU and still misses the hardest cases, so brute-force sampling has hit diminishing returns.
quote: one NVIDIA B300, the state-of-the-art hardware, needs several hours to complete 512 traces for a single AIME-2025 problem on vLLM (Kwon et al., 2023) with Qwen3-8B model (Team, 2025) while still failing on the hardest instances.

problem_sentence: Even when a search method generates far fewer tokens in total, the wall-clock time barely improves because a few surviving traces run very long and decoding them is sequential.
quote: This distributional shift explains why token savings do not directly translate into proportional latency reductions. Although Gambit minimizes redundant token generation via prefix sharing, it allocates more compute to continuing high-quality trajectories, resulting in a higher fraction of long-running traces.

problem_sentence: Long reasoning traces fill the GPU's attention cache quickly, and the serving engine then makes new requests wait in line, roughly tripling how long each question takes.
quote: Standard parallel sampling launches many concurrent traces, but long contexts quickly saturate the KV cache. As illustrated in Figure 3, this forces inference engines such as vLLM (Kwon et al., 2023) or SGLang (Zheng et al., 2024) to severely queue requests, heavily inflating end-to-end latency.

problem_sentence: Fast failover only covers software crashes in the inference worker; a GPU hardware fault or driver reset still forces a slow cold restart of the inference engine.
quote: Belayer's shadow-worker handover targets worker-local software failures and does not guarantee warm recovery from CUDA context corruption, driver resets, GPU hardware faults, or failures of the weight/KV-cache servers.

problem_sentence: After a worker crash, the cached attention state for in-flight requests is thrown away and recomputed because there is no way to tell which cache entries were fully written before the failure.
quote: Recovering the KV cache without refilling would require fine-grained consistency tracking, which we leave to future work.

problem_sentence: The framework lowers setup cost but the paper does not show that it reaches competitive task performance, so whether its generic environment handling is enough for strong agents is untested.
quote: We do not aim for state of the art on any benchmark; reaching it would take dedicated data and environment engineering, which is orthogonal to the framework.

problem_sentence: The system was only tested on short trajectories and limited write patterns, so it is unknown how many environments per machine it really supports when agents write heavily or run for a long time.
quote: Broader mutation workloads, longer trajectories, and concurrency sweeps are needed to characterize the remaining sharing boundary, stress state isolation under diverse write patterns, and determine how these gains translate into achievable environment density.

problem_sentence: Whether to run prompt processing and token generation on separate GPUs, and how to split GPUs between them, has no fixed best answer; it flips with batch size and workload, so a static serving configuration is always wrong some of the time.
quote: Disaggregation trades reduced interference for KV-transfer overhead and a partitioned GPU pool; when transfer overhead dominates or either pool bottlenecks, colocation can be preferable. Second, the optimal PD ratio depends on the workload. No single ratio is best across batch sizes

problem_sentence: While agents wait on tool calls they occupy no GPU, so the decode GPUs run with smaller batches than planned and, in a split prefill/decode design, cannot fill the gap with other work.
quote: During environment interactions, trajectories sit in neither queue, so the effective decode batch size drops. Unlike colocation, disaggregated decode GPUs cannot reuse idle cycles for prefill, so environment interactions reduce decode throughput.

problem_sentence: The system's own cost estimate for borrowing GPUs was wrong early in training, so its safety gate skipped borrowing when it would have helped; the decision quality depends on calibrating overhead estimates online.
quote: For Qwen3-8B, the initial estimate of toggle overhead was too high, so the gate conservatively disabled toggle during several early phases that would have benefited from it; the gated configuration therefore achieves +92.3%, slightly below the +93.6% of ungated toggle.

problem_sentence: While an agent waits for a tool call, other rollouts push its cached context out of GPU memory, so when it resumes the model must recompute the whole prefix, and the very trick that fills GPU idle time makes this thrashing worse.
quote: A trajectory may first generate, suspend during tool execution, and later resume after its KV Cache has already been evicted by other active trajectories [6, 28, 31]. This causes repeated recomputation overhead. What's worse, the action-level scheduling, while effective for eliminating GPU idle time, increases the number of interleaved active trajectories and thereby aggravates this problem.

problem_sentence: Even in the simplest idealized setting, deciding the best order to run rollouts so that training batches complete earliest is computationally intractable, so any practical scheduler is a heuristic.
quote: Computing an optimal group-completion schedule is NP-hard under this model, even with two identical unit-capacity GPU slots, single-request groups, known processing times, no environment delays, and sufficient KV-cache capacity.

problem_sentence: Computing gradients early requires holding partial gradient accumulators in memory until the whole batch is done, so the speedup costs several extra gigabytes per training GPU.
quote: Starting work early also means keeping partial gradient state until each group or batch closes, which exchanges trainer memory for wall time.

problem_sentence: The speedup depends on the objective and the workload: it is near two times only when rollout and learning take about equal time, and shrinks when one side dominates or when the loss needs whole-group information.
quote: Objectives whose gradient inputs resolve early, such as turn-level OPD, leave more learner work to overlap with rollout than objectives that wait on group-level signals, and the benefit is largest when rollout and learner work take comparable time.

problem_sentence: The exact early-gradient trick has only been worked out for two loss functions and tested on single-node setups, so other RL objectives and multi-node clusters are not covered.
quote: identifying readiness units for other objectives would extend exact gradient streaming beyond GRPO and OPD. Scaling the same principle to multi-node training and a broader set of agentic workloads is a natural next step.

problem_sentence: The speedup model assumes the trainer can always accept a new gradient job the moment it is ready and that jobs never slow each other down, which may not hold on crowded GPUs.
quote: It assumes enough device memory to admit each source when it becomes ready. In particular, service times do not change with concurrent rollout activity or with the schedule's choice of release times.

problem_sentence: When rollout GPUs sit in a different datacenter from the trainer, shipping the full new model weights after every update takes minutes to over an hour, which is longer than the training step itself.
quote: A cross-cluster transfer of a 120B model's 247.2 GB checkpoint through object storage takes 750 s, and at the 1T scale of models like Kimi K2 [14], such a transfer takes 87.5 min (Figure 1).

problem_sentence: Almost all the bytes moved during a weight update are weights that did not change, because low-precision storage rounds most small optimizer updates away.
quote: Other reports give element change rates of 1.5-2.0% in Qwen3 RL [26] and average deltas of 1.98% of a 1,024 GiB checkpoint [5]. A full-checkpoint transfer thus spends 98-99% of its bytes on unchanged elements.

problem_sentence: Computing and applying the compressed difference takes time of its own, and if that is not overlapped with the transfer the savings vanish; tying trainer and rollout clusters into one collective also means one failed machine stalls everyone.
quote: The next rollout batch waits for the complete update, so without overlap, delta construction and application can offset the transfer savings. A cross-cluster collective couples receiver membership to the training cluster and introduces timeouts upon failure [23].

problem_sentence: To know which weights changed, the trainer must keep an extra full copy of the previous weights in CPU memory, about one whole checkpoint spread across training machines.
quote: The baseline uses host memory, not GPU memory. Beyond one copy of the source weights in the trackers, it holds the canonical tensors of residual tasks, which are 3.69% of the Qwen3-30B-A3B checkpoint and 3.01% of the Nemotron-3-Ultra-550B-A55B checkpoint.

problem_sentence: The whole approach relies on very few weights changing per step, which holds at tiny learning rates but weakens with larger learning rates or early in training, so the savings are not guaranteed for every recipe.
quote: an update changes a stored BF16 value only when it crosses a rounding boundary (Figure 3), so larger learning rates and early training steps change more stored values.

problem_sentence: Even with compression, pushing a weight update to a trillion-parameter rollout fleet across clusters still takes several minutes, and almost all of that time is raw network transport that no further compression removes.
quote: refit latency grows with checkpoint size, from 8.3-14.5 s at 30B to 150-300 s at 1T (Figure 10). At 5%, the relay tree beats object storage at every size, and its advantage grows from 1.13x at 30B to 1.36x at 1T.

problem_sentence: The protocol recovers from crashes and lost messages but assumes nobody tampers with the data, and when automatic retries run out a human has to step in.
quote: Owners, receivers, transports, and coordinators may crash or lose messages (Table B.2), but they do not act maliciously, and channels are trusted or encrypted.
